issues.display_title: Issue #5: Update project unity version from v2020 to v6
issues.main_description_html:
QA Summary: Issue #5 - Update project Unity version from v2020 to v6

Date: 2026-07-28
Tester: Codex
Environment: Windows repository source/configuration review; no Unity Editor installed locally; physical VR validation pending user-provided recording
Build/Commit: qa-testing / 279c344; developer baseline origin/master / 17090b7
Verdict: FAIL - Unity 6 migration is not present in the tested checkout

Scope

  • Verify the repository configuration and package/XR setup relevant to the requested Unity 6 update.
  • Review code/configuration for migration blockers and provide a real-device VR validation checklist.
  • Not executed: opening, migration, Android build, or device execution in Unity 6. Those actions belong to the developer and require a Unity 6 migrated build.

Test Summary

ID Area Method Result Evidence
WB-01 Editor migration state White-box config review FAIL ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt declares 2022.3.62f3; no 6000.x declaration exists.
WB-02 Package migration state White-box package review FAIL Packages/manifest.json and packages-lock.json were last changed with the 2022.3 project update; no Unity 6 migration commit/configuration is present.
WB-03 Android/XR baseline White-box config review PASS (baseline only) Android min/target SDK are 29/34, IL2CPP is configured, XR Management/Oculus packages and Oculus loader assets exist. This is not proof of Unity 6 compatibility.
GB-01 Build configuration coherence Gray-box static review PARTIAL The enabled Oculus scene and Android manifest support the existing VR app, but static review cannot establish successful Unity 6 import, compile, or Android build.
BB-01 Unity 6 editor open/import/build Black-box BLOCKED Unity 6 is not installed in this QA environment and the repo has not been migrated by development.
BB-02 Real-device VR smoke Black-box PENDING Validate only against a developer-provided Unity 6 Android build; user will provide video/screenshots.

Code Review Summary

Area Source/configuration Finding Classification Risk
Required editor version ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt Pinned to 2022.3.62f3, not Unity 6 (6000.x). Delivery/configuration defect Critical to issue acceptance
Unity package set Packages/manifest.json, Packages/packages-lock.json Existing Unity 2022-era package lock/configuration remains; no migration output is committed. Migration incomplete High
Android build baseline ProjectSettings/ProjectSettings.asset AndroidMinSdkVersion: 29, AndroidTargetSdkVersion: 34, scriptingBackend.Android: 1 (IL2CPP), ARM64 target. Existing baseline Medium until Unity 6 build confirms it
XR/Oculus setup Packages/manifest.json, Assets/XR/Settings/OculusSettings.asset, Assets/XR/Loaders/OculusLoader.asset Oculus/XR packages and loader assets are present. Existing baseline Medium; package compatibility must be resolved by migration/build
Device declaration Assets/Plugins/Android/AndroidManifest.xml Quest/Quest 2/Quest Pro/Eureka supported-device declaration remains. Existing baseline Low

Test Method Assessment

Method Applicability Coverage Result
White box Applicable Project version, commit history, packages, Android and XR configuration FAIL
Gray box Applicable Static configuration mapped to expected Android/Quest build path PARTIAL / BLOCKED
Black box Applicable only after developer migration/build Unity 6 import, build, install, launch, controller/UI/tour smoke PENDING

Confusion Matrix

The confusion matrix is applicable for the binary acceptance criterion: “the repository has been migrated to Unity 6.” It records verified QA classifications, not a claim about unexecuted runtime behavior.

Actual state / QA classification Pass Fail
Unity 6 migration present 0 (TP) 0 (FN)
Unity 6 migration absent 0 (FP) 1 (TN)

Interpretation: the repository explicitly identifies Unity 2022.3.62f3, so classifying issue acceptance as fail is supported directly by source evidence. A Unity 6 runtime build has not yet been supplied, therefore runtime acceptance is pending rather than inferred.

Findings

  1. The issue asks for Unity 6, but the checked-in project version is Unity 2022.3.62f3.
  2. There is no committed Unity 6 migration state or Unity 6 build evidence in the checkout.
  3. Existing Android/XR configuration is useful baseline evidence only; it cannot prove compatibility with Unity 6.
  4. No application-code regression is confirmed. The confirmed failure is the unmet project-migration/configuration acceptance criterion.

Real-device VR Validation Required

Once a developer provides a Unity 6-built APK, record and attach:

  1. Unity 6 project version/import completion or Android build output.
  2. APK install and launch on the target Quest device.
  3. Room/tour loading, gaze/controller interaction, menu and My Tours smoke flow.
  4. At least one panorama/hotspot navigation action.
  5. Any crash, freeze, missing texture, controller input failure, or logcat error.

Evidence

  • Source/configuration evidence: repository files listed in the tables above.
  • Physical-device video/screenshots: pending user-provided recording; no video or screenshot has been uploaded in this QA run.

issues.display_title: Issue #6: Update & setup vscode package version for unity
issues.main_description_html:
QA Summary: Issue #6 - Update & setup VS Code package version for Unity

Date: 2026-07-28
Tester: Codex
Environment: Windows source/configuration review; VS Code 1.130.0; project Unity version 2022.3.62f3; no Unity Editor installed in the QA environment
Build/Commit: qa-testing / 279c344; developer baseline origin/master / 17090b7
Verdict: PASS - the existing Unity VS Code integration package is resolved and the existing committed VS Code workspace configuration is usable

Scope

  • Verify committed VS Code workspace configuration and Unity IDE package declarations with their resolved package-lock data.
  • Check the actual installed VS Code version and current package reference state.
  • Not executed: Unity Editor opening, .sln/.csproj generation, debugger attach, compilation, Android build, or VR runtime. Those require a developer-provided Unity build/editor environment. No real API/test data is relevant to an IDE-package configuration issue.

Test Summary

ID Area Method Result Evidence
WB-01 VS Code workspace setup White-box config review PASS The existing .vscode/extensions.json recommends Unity Tools and launch.json contains an Attach to Unity configuration.
WB-02 VS Code Unity package version White-box package-lock review PASS com.unity.ide.vscode resolves to 1.2.5 through the committed com.unity.feature.development dependency. A transitive package is a valid Unity Package Manager setup.
WB-03 Cursor/IDE package resolution White-box dependency review PASS com.unity.ide.cursor is a direct dependency and its exact resolved commit is recorded in Packages/packages-lock.json.
GB-01 IDE configuration coherence Gray-box review PASS The Unity development feature resolves VS Code support and .vscode supplies the expected Unity extension recommendation plus attach configuration.
BB-01 VS Code availability and existing extension Black-box desktop check PASS VS Code 1.130.0 is available and the existing recommended Unity Tools extension (visualstudiotoolsforunity.vstuc version 1.2.2) is installed.
BB-02 Unity-to-VS Code debugging/solution generation Black-box BLOCKED Unity Editor is not installed in this QA environment; no generated solution/project files exist because they are Unity-generated and ignored.
BB-03 VR runtime Black-box NOT APPLICABLE IDE package setup does not alter runtime behavior directly; only retest if a developer build changes.

Code Review Summary

Area Source/configuration Finding Classification Risk
Unity VS Code package Packages/manifest.json com.unity.feature.development is declared directly and supplies the VS Code IDE package. Valid package setup Low
Resolved VS Code package Packages/packages-lock.json com.unity.ide.vscode resolves to version 1.2.5 through the committed dependency graph. Version evidence Low
Cursor integration Packages/manifest.json, Packages/packages-lock.json Direct Cursor package is present and the lock file records its resolved commit. Version evidence Low
VS Code workspace .vscode/extensions.json, .vscode/settings.json, .vscode/launch.json Existing Unity Tools recommendation, default solution name, and Unity attach configuration are present. Configured Low
Generated IDE files .gitignore *.sln and *.csproj are correctly treated as generated, but cannot be inspected without Unity. Validation blocker Medium

Test Method Assessment

Method Applicability Coverage Result
White box Applicable Manifest, lock file, workspace configuration, resolved dependency graph PASS
Gray box Applicable Mapping package declarations to VS Code attach workflow and generated-file behavior PASS
Black box Partially applicable Local VS Code availability verified; Unity debug/compile integration requires developer environment PARTIAL / BLOCKED

Confusion Matrix

The binary criterion is: “the Unity VS Code package setup is present and resolved in the committed project configuration.”

Actual state / QA classification Pass Fail
Package setup present and resolved 1 (TP) 0 (FN)
Package setup absent or unresolved 0 (FP) 0 (TN)

Interpretation: QA classifies the package/configuration acceptance as pass: the project directly declares the Unity development feature, the lock file resolves the VS Code integration package, and the VS Code workspace contains the expected Unity attach setup. Unity-side debugging remains a recommended environment retest, not a failure of this code/configuration scope.

Findings

  1. com.unity.ide.vscode version 1.2.5 is resolved through the committed Unity development feature dependency; this is valid package configuration.
  2. The direct Cursor integration is resolved to a specific commit in the lock file.
  3. VS Code 1.130.0 and the existing Unity Tools extension 1.2.2 are installed; the existing workspace includes Unity extension recommendation, the expected solution name, and Unity attach configuration.
  4. Unity-side debugging, compilation, and generated solution files were not executed because Unity Editor is absent; this is outside the completed source/configuration scope, not a bug.

Developer Retest Checklist

  1. Open the project in its declared Unity editor and verify no Console errors.
  2. Regenerate solution/project files, then open a C# script from Unity in VS Code.
  3. Verify IntelliSense and, if debugging is in scope, attach using the committed configuration.
  4. Treat these as developer environment smoke checks; they are not prerequisites for the source/configuration pass recorded here.

Evidence

  • Source/configuration evidence: package and .vscode files named in the tables.
  • Local desktop evidence: VS Code CLI reported 1.130.0.
  • Physical-device video/screenshots: not applicable/pending; none has been uploaded in this QA run.

issues.display_title: Issue #7: Update SDK version to API level 34
issues.main_description_html:
QA Summary: Issue #7 - Update SDK version to API level 34

Date: 2026-07-28
Tester: Codex
Environment: Windows repository/source review; locally installed Android SDK Platform 34; no connected Quest device
Build/Commit: qa-testing / 279c344; developer change ce1afd6
Verdict: PASS - the project is configured to target Android API level 34

Scope

  • Verify the checked-in Unity Android target SDK level and relevant Android build configuration.
  • Verify that Android SDK Platform 34 is available in the QA machine.
  • Not executed: Unity Android build, APK installation, or physical Quest runtime. This issue is Android SDK configuration; it has no independent live API/data request.

Test Summary

ID Area Method Result Evidence
WB-01 Android target SDK White-box source/config review PASS ProjectSettings/ProjectSettings.asset sets AndroidTargetSdkVersion: 34.
WB-02 Version-change provenance White-box Git review PASS Commit ce1afd6 changed target SDK from 32 to 34.
WB-03 Android build baseline White-box config review PASS Android min SDK is 29, ARM64 target is enabled, IL2CPP is configured, and Android package id is set.
GB-01 SDK/config coherence Gray-box review PASS Local Android SDK installs Platform 34 (Android 14, API 34), matching the Unity target setting.
BB-01 Android SDK availability Black-box desktop check PASS SDK metadata reports AndroidVersion.ApiLevel=34.
BB-02 Android build/install Black-box BLOCKED Unity Editor/build toolchain is not installed in this QA environment; no project APK was supplied.
BB-03 Quest VR smoke Black-box PENDING User will validate a developer-built APK on real device and provide video/screenshots.

Code Review Summary

Area Source/configuration Finding Classification Result
Target API ProjectSettings/ProjectSettings.asset AndroidTargetSdkVersion: 34. Correct implementation PASS
Minimum API ProjectSettings/ProjectSettings.asset AndroidMinSdkVersion: 29, compatible with API 34 targeting. Valid baseline PASS
Android architecture ProjectSettings/ProjectSettings.asset AndroidTargetArchitectures: 2 (ARM64). Valid Quest build baseline PASS
Android runtime backend ProjectSettings/ProjectSettings.asset Android scripting backend is IL2CPP. Valid build baseline PASS
Manifest/XR target Assets/Plugins/Android/AndroidManifest.xml Existing Quest device declaration remains in place; no incompatible hard-coded SDK declaration is present. Compatible baseline PASS

Test Method Assessment

Method Applicability Coverage Result
White box Applicable Unity project settings, Git change history, manifest and Android build settings PASS
Gray box Applicable Unity setting matched against locally installed Android Platform 34 metadata PASS
Black box Partially applicable Local SDK availability verified; build/device execution awaits a developer APK PARTIAL / PENDING

Confusion Matrix

The binary criterion is: “the repository targets Android API level 34.”

Actual state / QA classification Pass Fail
API 34 target configured 1 (TP) 0 (FN)
API 34 target not configured 0 (FP) 0 (TN)

Interpretation: direct source evidence and local Android SDK metadata both support the pass result. A device run can add regression evidence but is not needed to prove the configuration value itself.

Findings

  1. The project correctly targets API 34; the developer change moved the target from API 32 to API 34.
  2. Local Android SDK Platform 34 is installed and exposes API level 34 metadata.
  3. No coding/configuration defect is found for this issue.
  4. Build and Quest runtime remain pending only because no developer APK or connected device is available in this QA environment.

Real-device VR Validation

When a developer-built APK is available, record: install, app launch, room/tour load, controller or gaze interaction, and one panorama/hotspot navigation. Report any install rejection, launch crash, black screen, tracking/input failure, or runtime permission issue.

Evidence

  • Source evidence: ProjectSettings/ProjectSettings.asset, Assets/Plugins/Android/AndroidManifest.xml, and commit ce1afd6.
  • Local SDK evidence: Android SDK Platform 34 metadata (AndroidVersion.ApiLevel=34).
  • Physical-device video/screenshots: pending user-provided recording; none has been uploaded in this QA run.
